summary: An excerpt from a fiction novel (Book 4, part 36) following Anda and her leader Lucy, who run paid in-game missions in a game world centered on Fahrenheit Island. Anda has suddenly gained real cash from the work, which makes her popular at school, and the two take on a mission near home, clearing sniper lookouts with BFG weapons supplied by non-player-character armorers. Anda questions why anyone would pay so much for these missions, and Lucy jokes it may be rich gamers pranking each other, then reasons about money by comparing a frappuccino's worth to a world of people living on a dollar a day.
one_line: Anda and Lucy take a lucrative paid in-game mission in a fantasy game, and Anda questions who is paying them.
key_facts: Anda now has pocket-money for the first time in her life, and the cash she earns lets her buy snacks outside the 500 meter sugar-free zone around her school.
Anda is described as the richest kid she knows, and she distributes handsful of Curly snacks to her schoolmates.
Lucy's voice in Anda's ear through the voicelink is a constant companion when Anda is not on Fahrenheit Island.
The Fahrenheit armorers, non-player-characters, have learned to recognise Anda and keep the Clan's BFGs oiled and ready for her.
Lucy says that money talks and bullshit walks, and the narrator notes cash always beats gold and experience beats experience points.
Anda uses a scrying spell to spot the first round of sniper/lookouts, and Lucy fires BFG rounds at the hilltops before they get into bow range.
Anda asks Lucy, who she addresses as Sarge, why anyone would pay them cash for these missions.
Lucy suspects that two rich gamers who pay their butlers to craft for them all day may be paying them as a prank.
Lucy says that most of the world lives on like a dollar a day, and she spends five dollars every day on a frappuccino.
Lucy says her dad sends her mom three thousand a month in child-support, which is a hundred bucks a day.
Lucy claims that if a day's money in the game is a hundred, her frappuccino is worth like five hundred dollars.
Lucy's dad loved an old TV show and makes the same joke about her name every visitation day.
